subject: Runway convergence: exec actions & account playbook for QBR
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@acme.com>, sales@acme.com
Date: 2026-08-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Runway convergence: exec actions & account playbook for QBR

Team —

We're two weeks out from the QBR readout and I want to lock the runway view for the accounts we're presenting. Goal for this thread: consolidate forecasts into a single master, confirm owner-level ask for each account, and surface any exec-level risks so we can prep mitigations.

Asks:
- Please update the attached QBR_runway_master.xlsx with your final best-case / commit / close dates by EOD Mon 8/31. Use the "Owner Notes" column for any contextual bullets.
- For any account where probability moved +/- 15% since last week, add a 1–2 line rationale.
- If an account needs a leadership escalation (SLA, pricing exception, slow procurement), mark it with "ESCALATE" and include one-sentence proposed ask.

Quick context on priority accounts:
- Acme Inc. — large ARR; procurement timeline uncertain, legal OK but procurement delay (Julia included).
- BetaCorp — steady; needs final SOW and small PO sign-off.
- Gamma Systems — at-risk; technical objection on privacy that CS is triaging.

I'll own the consolidated deck slide and the exec summary. Marissa, can you bring the one-pager for Acme? Tessa, please flag any accounts you recommend we escalate to the exec table. Karthik, please run the consolidated forecast numbers and call out material changes vs. last quarter.

Attachments: QBR_runway_master.xlsx (sheet tabs: raw-inputs, owner-rollup, executive-summary).

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Manager, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

- Risk: procurement requires our data residency language; legal cleared earlier but procurement is slower than expected.
- Near-term next step: Julia's procurement lead committed to a response by 9/2.

BetaCorp (owner: Marissa)
- PO expected; waiting on final SOW edits (engineering).
- Revenue sizing unchanged.

I added a short one-pager for Acme to the Drive (link below) and attached ACME_onepager.pdf. Will update if procurement moves.

Agree with Marissa — noting Gamma Systems as an item I recommend we escalate.

Gamma Systems (owner: TBD)
- Issue: technical objection around on-prem key management and auditability. CS has a running log; I exported the risk items into Gamma_risk_log.csv and added a proposed mitigation: offer a 30-day pilot with customer-managed keys and an SRE support slot.
- Proposed ask for execs: approve a pilot SLA and a one-time engineering allocation (estimated 2 engineer-weeks).

If we think Gamma is worth the pilot, I can draft the exec note.

Tessa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Thanks — I've pulled a consolidated view and included preliminary numbers below (I put the full sheet into the attached master). These are top-line owner rollups only — leave item-level details in the owner notes.

Consolidated preview (owner rollup):
- Acme Inc.: Best-case $1,200,000 / Commit $900,000 / Close: 2026-10-15
- BetaCorp: Best-case $280,000 / Commit $250,000 / Close: 2026-09-09
- Gamma Systems: Best-case $420,000 / Commit $210,000 / Close: TBD (needs pilot)
- Other (combined smaller deals): Best-case $320,000 / Commit $220,000

Net Best-case: $2,220,000
Net Commit: $1,580,000

Material movements vs last snapshot: Acme down 15% probability due to procurement delay; Gamma moved to "at-risk" (-30%) pending pilot decision.

Action items:
1) Owners to finalize owner notes + commit/close by EOD Mon 8/31.
2) Marissa to confirm Acme PO status on 9/2 and update master when received.
3) Tessa to draft a short exec escalation note for Gamma if we agree to pilot.
4) Ben to assemble slides for exec summary by 9/3.

I'll circulate the cleaned rollup after I receive the final owner inputs.

Karthik
